header.title: Global central banks resume hiking but Nomura sees far fewer hikes than markets price

s01_bottom_line.text: Nomura forecasts a resumption of rate hikes (Fed one hike in December then hold through 2027; ECB two hikes to 3.00%; BOJ two hikes to 1.75%; none for BoE/BoC) but significantly fewer than markets price. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩
Nomura frames its forecasts as diverging from consensus, implying markets have over-priced hikes given rates are near neutral and inflation is cost-push.

A large gap between Nomura's dovish-relative forecasts and market pricing across multiple central banks signals potential rate-market mispricing worth investigating across rates and FX-sensitive equities.

items.text: Nomura has added rate hikes to its global monetary policy forecasts but still forecasts significantly fewer hikes than markets are pricing.
Nomura expects two more BOJ hikes vs market consensus of four or more. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩
Nomura expects two more ECB hikes in December 2026 and March 2027, vs market expectations of two to three more. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩
Nomura expects another 25bp Fed hike in December. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩
Nomura expects the ECB to hike in December 2026 and March 2027, bringing the deposit rate to 3.00%. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩
Nomura expects BOJ hikes in December 2026 and March 2027 to 1.75% in its main scenario with 60% probability. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩
